title: Le temps qui passe
intro: 25 essential words for talking about time: now, soon, already, still, never, often, sometimes, for a long time, the beginning and the end, the past, the present and the future… and the day before yesterday (**avant-hier**) and the day after tomorrow (**après-demain**).

words.def: En ce moment : pas avant, pas après.
words.def_en: At this moment: not before, not after.

examples.en: I haven't got time now.
Come now, please!
He lives in Lyon now.
See you soon!
The holidays are coming soon.
It's going to rain soon.

words.def: Avant maintenant ; plus tôt que prévu.

examples.en: Have you already finished?
It's already midnight!
Have you ever been to Paris?

words.en: again; still; more; (pas encore) not yet
words.def: Une autre fois. Aussi : comme avant, toujours.
words.def_en: One more time. Also: as before, still.

examples.en: You're late again!
It's still raining.
I haven't eaten yet.

words.def: Tout le temps. Aussi : encore maintenant.
words.def_en: All the time. Also: even now.

examples.en: Hugo is always late.
Do you still live in Lyon?
I'll always love you.
I never drink coffee.
He's never been to Paris.
Never!
I often go to the cinema.
Does it often rain in Lyon?
Grandma often phones.

words.def_en: Some of the time, not always.

examples.en: Sometimes I work on Saturdays.
Hugo is sometimes on time!
It sometimes snows in March.
I waited a long time.
Are you staying long in Paris?
A long time ago…
Wait a moment!
At the moment, I'm working a lot.

examples.fr: C'est le meilleur **moment** de la journée.
examples.en: It's the best moment of the day.
At the beginning, it was hard.

examples.fr: Le **début** du film est un peu long.
examples.en: The start of the film is a bit slow.
I'm leaving at the beginning of January.
It's the end of the film.

examples.fr: À la **fin** de la journée, je suis fatigué.
examples.en: At the end of the day, I'm tired.
I'm leaving at the end of January.

words.note: Not to be confused with the adjective **fin, fine** (thin, fine).

words.def: Soixante minutes. Aussi : le moment de la journée : il est huit heures.
words.def_en: Sixty minutes. Also: the time of day: it's eight o'clock.

examples.en: What time is it?
The film lasts two hours.
You're on time!

words.note: **à l'heure** = on time; **tout à l'heure** = in a little while, or a little while ago.

examples.en: I'll be there in five minutes!
Just a minute, please!

examples.fr: Le bus passe toutes les dix **minutes**.
examples.en: The bus comes every ten minutes.

words.def: Un tout petit temps : il y en a soixante dans une minute.
words.def_en: A very short time: there are sixty in a minute.

examples.en: Wait a second!

examples.fr: Il a couru cent mètres en douze **secondes**.
examples.en: He ran a hundred metres in twelve seconds.
Ten seconds to midnight!
This church is eight centuries old.

examples.fr: Nous sommes au vingt et unième **siècle**.
examples.en: We're in the twenty-first century.

examples.fr: Ça fait un **siècle** que je ne t'ai pas vu !
examples.en: I haven't seen you for ages!

words.def: Le temps qui vient, après maintenant.
words.def_en: The time to come, after now.

examples.fr: Dans le **futur**, on habitera peut-être sur la lune.
examples.en: In the future, perhaps we'll live on the moon.
The future is in your hands!

examples.fr: Aujourd'hui, on apprend le **futur** : je parlerai, tu parleras…
examples.en: Today we're learning the future tense: I will speak, you will speak…

words.note: **l'avenir** = your future (your life, your plans); **le futur** = the future in general, and the tense.

words.def: Qui est là, maintenant. Le présent : le temps d'aujourd'hui.
words.def_en: Here, now. Le présent: the time we're living in.

examples.en: All the pupils are present.
You have to live in the present!
'Je parle' is the present tense.

words.def: Le temps d'avant, qui est fini.
words.def_en: The time before now, which is over.

examples.en: That's in the past, let's not talk about it any more.
Grandma likes talking about the past.

examples.fr: Dans le **passé**, il n'y avait pas d'internet.
examples.en: In the past, there was no internet.
I'm leaving the day after tomorrow.
Shall we meet the day after tomorrow?
Today's Monday; the day after tomorrow is Wednesday.
I saw him the day before yesterday.
The day before yesterday, the weather was lovely.
The parcel arrived the day before yesterday.

words.en: the next day, the day after
words.def: Le jour qui suit un autre jour.
words.def_en: The day that follows another day.

examples.en: The next day, it was raining.

examples.fr: Je suis arrivé le **lendemain** de Noël.
examples.en: I arrived the day after Christmas.

examples.fr: Le **lendemain** de la fête, tout le monde est fatigué.
examples.en: The day after the party, everyone is tired.

words.note: **le lendemain** (the next day, in a story) vs **demain** (tomorrow, from today).

examples.en: I saw this film recently.
They recently moved house.
Recently, Hugo has been doing sport.

words.en: in a little while; a little while ago
words.def: Dans un petit moment, ou il y a un petit moment.
words.def_en: In a short while, or a short while ago.

examples.en: See you later!
I'll call you in a bit.
He was here a little while ago.

examples.fr: Ne parlez pas tous **en même temps** !
examples.en: Don't all talk at once!

examples.fr: Je mange et je regarde la télé **en même temps**.
examples.en: I eat and watch TV at the same time.
They arrived at the same time.

story.title: Le réveillon
story.en: New Year's Eve at Léa and Sophie's: everyone waits for midnight.

lines.fr: Le trente et un décembre, c'est le réveillon du Nouvel An. Les amis sont chez Léa et Sophie.
lines.en: On 31 December, it's New Year's Eve. The friends are at Léa and Sophie's.

lines.fr: Quelle semaine ! Récemment, il y a eu beaucoup de surprises : avant-hier, Hugo est passé à la télé, et hier, c'était ma fête !
lines.en: What a week! There have been lots of surprises recently: the day before yesterday, Hugo was on TV, and yesterday was my party!

lines.fr: Et maintenant, le réveillon ! Je suis toujours fatigué, mais je suis content.
lines.en: And now, New Year's Eve! I'm still tired, but I'm happy.

lines.fr: Il est déjà onze heures. Dans une heure, c'est la fin de l'année !
lines.en: It's already eleven o'clock. In an hour, it's the end of the year!

lines.fr: Le début d'une nouvelle année… J'adore ce moment.
lines.en: The beginning of a new year… I love this moment.

lines.fr: Parfois, je pense au passé… Et souvent, je pense au futur !
lines.en: Sometimes I think about the past… And I often think about the future!

lines.fr: Moi, je pense au présent : où sont les crêpes ?
lines.en: I'm thinking about the present: where are the crêpes?

lines.fr: Tu as mangé tout à l'heure ! Tu manges encore ?
lines.en: You ate a little while ago! You're eating again?

lines.fr: Je n'ai jamais assez mangé le soir du réveillon. C'est une tradition depuis des siècles !
lines.en: I never eat enough on New Year's Eve. It's a centuries-old tradition!

lines.fr: Léa téléphone longtemps à ses parents, à Paris. Lou passe les vacances chez sa grande sœur, et elle ne dort pas encore : elle veut voir minuit !
lines.en: Léa has a long phone call with her parents in Paris. Lou is spending the holidays at her big sister's, and she isn't asleep yet: she wants to see midnight!

lines.fr: Léa, c'est bientôt minuit ? Il reste combien de minutes ?
lines.en: Léa, is it nearly midnight? How many minutes are left?

lines.fr: Encore quinze minutes, ma puce. Tu es toujours debout ?
lines.en: Fifteen more minutes, sweetie. You're still up?

lines.fr: À minuit moins une, tout le monde [compte|compter] les secondes en même temps : « Dix, neuf, huit… »
lines.en: At one minute to midnight, everyone counts down the seconds together: 'Ten, nine, eight…'
'… three, two, one… Happy New Year!'

lines.fr: On s'embrasse, on rit. Le lendemain, tout le monde dort jusqu'à midi… et après-demain, c'est le retour au travail !
lines.en: Everyone hugs and laughs. The next day, everyone sleeps until noon… and the day after tomorrow, it's back to work!

lines.fr: Déjà ? Les vacances passent toujours trop vite !
lines.en: Already? Holidays always go too fast!
